summary: formatting-subtitles-for-claude postinstall shells out to a dependency-shipped payload disguised as JavaScript
details: The npm package formatting-subtitles-for-claude@1.0.1 declares a postinstall hook `sh./node_modules/unicode-title-normalizer/x.js && exit 0` and lists `unicode-title-normalizer@1.1.0` as a dependency. The shipped files (index.js/cli.js) implement a benign Unicode/color title normalizer and never reference x.js; the actual install-time code lives in the separately resolved dependency and is executed by `sh`, not by node, so despite the `.js` extension the file is interpreted as a shell script. Installing the package causes npm to resolve that dependency and run its x.js contents as a shell script on the installer's host, with the lure package name targeting users working with Claude. The host-package tarball is a thin stub that hides the real payload one dependency indirection away and uses a `.js` suffix on a shell script to disguise it in casual file listings and from node-only scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
